q: Convert $54\,\text{km/h}$ to $\text{m/s}$ by substituting the units.
A cyclist's velocity falls uniformly from $12\,\text{m/s}$ to $4.0\,\text{m/s}$ in $4.0\,\text{s}$. What is the acceleration, and what does its sign tell you?
a: $a = \dfrac{\Delta v}{\Delta t} = \dfrac{4.0\,\text{m/s} - 12\,\text{m/s}}{4.0\,\text{s}} = -2.0\,\text{m/s}^2$. The sign is opposite to that of the velocity, so the speed decreases.
